scope: Reviewed the support-agent Kubernetes deployment: main harness (src/main.py, src/agent.py), authentication and credentials, tool definitions and MCP configuration, container image and Kubernetes manifests, policy enforcement, audit logging, budgets, kill switch, and telemetry. Did not review: test suites, internal database schemas in detail, production deployment configuration outside the repository.

evidence.note: Tool list is dynamic (npx -y), not pinned
zendesk-mcp has no version pin
@stripe/mcp has no version pin
gmail-mcp-server has no version pin
Tools loaded dynamically from servers with no allowlist filter
Only a simple blocklist, not a proper allowlist

findings.summary: Tool surface is not explicitly listed. MCP servers are loaded with dynamic versioning (npx -y) and tools are accepted from servers without an allowlist filter.
findings.next_step: Write an explicit tool inventory with task justification. Pin MCP server versions. Implement an allowlist filter that rejects unlisted tools.

evidence.note: Agent reuses the support rep's own OAuth token
User's bearer token passed through to downstream services
User token passed to MCP servers as environment variable
Uses shared service account for all replicas, not per-instance credential

findings.summary: The agent uses the support rep's own credentials for all downstream calls instead of using its own identity. This violates least-privilege: the agent inherits the rep's permissions.
findings.next_step: Give the agent its own workload identity (Kubernetes ServiceAccount or cloud IAM role). Use token exchange (RFC 8693) or credential issuing to give the agent narrowed credentials for each downstream service.

evidence.note: API key injected into system prompt: build_system_prompt includes INTERNAL_API_KEY
INTERNAL_API_KEY loaded from secret and visible to pod
No credential lifetime or rotation policy documented

findings.summary: The INTERNAL_API_KEY is injected into the system prompt where the model can see it. Credentials have no documented expiry or rotation policy.
findings.next_step: Remove credentials from prompts. Use service-to-service auth instead. Document and enforce short-lived credentials with rotation.

findings.summary: Because the agent uses the user's token, revoking the agent requires revoking the user's token (which cuts off the user). No separate agent identity exists to revoke independently.
findings.next_step: First implement B02 (agent identity). Then demonstrate independent revocation by disabling the agent's service account while the user's session stays active.

evidence.note: Policy is a simple blocklist: BLOCKED_TOOLS only
No check on arguments or target; just tool name
policy.allowed only checks tool name, not operation
issue_refund is a destructive action (sends money) with no approval gate
Can issue refunds through Stripe and send outside (email)

findings.summary: Destructive actions (refunds, email sends) are blocked only by tool name in a simple blocklist. No approval check exists. Arguments and targets are not validated. Model can use synonyms or workarounds.
findings.next_step: List all high-impact operations (deletes, refunds, sends outside). For each, implement an approval gate in the execution path that checks operation, target, and arguments at runtime.

evidence.note: No approval mechanism at all; only blocklist
Audit record has no approval_id field
issue_refund has no approval check

findings.summary: No approval mechanism exists. High-impact actions (refunds) are performed without approval from any reviewer.
findings.next_step: Implement an approval service. Before destructive actions, check that an approval record exists with: agent instance ID, exact operation, target, arguments, approver, and expiry.

evidence.note: max_steps, max_wall_seconds, max_total_tokens defined
RunBudget.check_step enforces limits outside model
TenantQuota enforces per-tenant and fleet daily spend caps
Budget checks before each model call

findings.summary: Budgets are enforced by the harness, not the model. Per-run and per-tenant limits exist. When exceeded, the run escalates rather than continuing.
findings.next_step: Runtime evidence needed: verify that actual budget exhaustion stops the run as configured.

evidence.note: Ingress limited to ingress-nginx namespace
Egress allows all (- {})

findings.summary: No documented inventory of systems and data stores the agent can reach. Egress is not restricted by NetworkPolicy. Infrastructure isolation cannot be verified from code alone.
findings.next_step: Write a list of all systems and datastores (Zendesk, Stripe, Gmail, Qdrant, Database, Redis). Test that the agent cannot reach production systems, admin systems, or other tenants' data from inside the pod.

evidence.note: Egress rule is empty dict - allows all egress
Can reach any npm registry, any Stripe endpoint, any Gmail endpoint
Can reach any Qdrant URL
No validation of MCP server endpoints

findings.summary: No egress allowlist. NetworkPolicy allows all egress (- {}). Agent can reach any external service.
findings.next_step: Create an egress allowlist by destination (Zendesk, Stripe, Gmail, Qdrant, etc.). Block metadata addresses (169.254.169.254) and loopback. Validate MCP server endpoints.

evidence.note: Image: ghcr.io/helpwise/support-agent:latest (mutable tag)
imagePullPolicy: Always pulls :latest every time
No signature verification policy

findings.summary: Container is referenced by mutable tag :latest, not by digest. No signature verification. Image is re-pulled every deployment attempt.
findings.next_step: Pin image by digest (image@sha256:...). Add image signature verification (Sigstore, Kyverno, or similar). Set imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent.

evidence.note: Based on python:3.12-slim (not distroless)
Includes curl, npm, nodejs which are not needed
No USER directive; runs as root
securityContext.privileged: true
runAsUser: 0
Missing allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: [ALL], seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

findings.summary: Container runs as root with privileged flag. Includes unnecessary shells and tools. Missing all Pod Security Standards restricted profile controls.
findings.next_step: Use distroless or minimal base image. Add USER directive. Remove curl, npm, apt. Add securityContext with runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: ALL, seccomp, and readOnlyRootFilesystem.

evidence.note: Harness loaded from config/agent.yaml (in repo)
System prompt loaded from prompts/system.md (in repo)
Deploy via kubectl apply -f k8s/ (no release process mentioned)

findings.summary: Harness and prompt are in version control, but no documented release process or branch protection rules are visible. Code review and release procedures need runtime verification.
findings.next_step: Verify: CODEOWNERS on harness and prompt files, branch protection blocking force-push, release CI/CD that traces deployed version to a reviewed commit.

evidence.note: Tool output joined with no type or size check: result.content with no validation
Tool results concatenated directly into context without sanitization
TicketEvent is validated by Pydantic, but content is trusted
KB search results returned without tenant or content validation

findings.summary: Tool and API outputs are used without content validation. No size limits on responses. No checks for injection payloads in retrieved documents or tool results.
findings.next_step: Implement content validation before tool results enter the model context. Add size limits. Check API responses for errors and hostile content.

evidence.note: Tool result formatted as 'Result of {tool_name}: {output}' and added to context
KB articles (untrusted content) formatted as 'KB: {doc}' and added to system context
system_template uses format with untrusted company_name from event.subdomain

findings.summary: Tool results and retrieved documents are concatenated into context as if they were instructions, not kept as separate untrusted data. KB articles are injected into the system context block.
findings.next_step: Format tool results and KB articles as tool-result role messages or user messages, not in the system prompt. Add source labels. Test injection payloads hidden in search results.

evidence.note: Tool arguments and details logged as JSON; could include secrets
No redaction policy visible

findings.summary: Tool arguments are logged, which could expose secrets. Redaction policies are not visible in code. Need runtime evidence that fake secrets don't appear in logs or model inputs.
findings.next_step: Recipe R03: return a fake secret in tool output, check that it's redacted before model receives it and doesn't appear in logs.

evidence.note: search_kb returns all matching documents without tenant filter
upsert_article takes tenant_id but no auth check
/kb/import endpoint has no authentication
Retrieved documents used without tenant verification

findings.summary: Retrieval corpus is shared across all tenants with no tenant access control. Any tenant's articles can be read by any agent. The /kb/import endpoint is unauthenticated.
findings.next_step: Add tenant filtering to search_kb() query. Require authentication on /kb/import. Store and enforce access permissions per chunk.

evidence.note: Each run is independent; run_ticket creates a new RunResult

findings.summary: The agent has no memory that persists between runs. Each ticket creates a fresh execution context.
findings.next_step: Governance approval of N/A status.

evidence.note: No cross-run memory; no persistence

findings.summary: No memory between runs means no provenance or cleanup is needed.
findings.next_step: Governance approval of N/A status.

evidence.note: context size logged per tool call decision: span.set_attribute('agent.context.size', context_tokens)
Method marked as 'measured'
action_span called with response.usage.input_tokens

findings.summary: Context size is measured and logged per tool call decision. Method is marked as measured.
findings.next_step: Runtime evidence: verify logged context sizes match the token counts in model responses.

evidence.note: Telemetry endpoint configured but rules not visible

findings.summary: No security-specific detection rules are visible in the repository. Telemetry is sent but monitoring rules are likely in separate infrastructure.
findings.next_step: Verify that security detection rules exist for: encoded payloads, unexpected egress, out-of-scope writes, repeated denials. Check alert routing to on-call security responder.

findings.summary: No sequence-aware detection rules are visible. Security monitoring happens outside the repo.
findings.next_step: Verify detection rules for suspicious action chains (multiple reads followed by send) and compare thresholds across context-size ranges.

findings.summary: No red-team or misalignment review evidence is in the repository. This likely happens outside code review.
findings.next_step: Verify that red-team testing has been done for evasive behaviors (splitting forbidden operations across calls) and that the results are recorded.

evidence.note: halted() checks Redis flag
Kill switch checked before every model call
Fail-closed: if Redis unavailable, assume halted
Kill switch uses Redis key outside agent control

findings.summary: Kill switch is checked before each model call. It uses an external Redis flag that the agent cannot write to. Fails closed if Redis is unavailable.
findings.next_step: Runtime drill: trigger the kill switch and measure actual stop time. Verify in-flight tool calls are cancelled.

evidence.note: halted() returns early from run_ticket loop

findings.summary: The kill switch stops new iterations but doesn't cancel in-flight tool calls or handle reconciliation of partial side effects.
findings.next_step: Recipe R12 drill: stop during a write, during a transaction, and after an outside action. Verify each is handled correctly.

evidence.note: Records each event (action, denial, error) with identity
Tool calls logged with tool name and arguments
Budget exceeded event logged
Final answer logged

findings.summary: Actions are logged to audit table with identity fields. Tool results and denials are recorded.
findings.next_step: Runtime evidence: rebuild a complete execution graph from audit logs and compare with a known run.

findings.summary: No automatic recovery, checkpointing, or replay logic is visible. Each run is independent.
findings.next_step: If recovery is added in future, verify idempotency keys and checkpoint tamper-resistance.

evidence.note: Agent reuses user's OAuth token
Uses shared serviceAccountName for all replicas
User token passed to downstream services

findings.summary: Agent has no separate identity; it uses the launching support rep's credentials for all downstream calls.
findings.next_step: First fix: implement B02. Give agent its own service account and use token exchange for downstream services.

evidence.note: identity dict built with all six fields
All six fields inserted into audit table
All six fields set as span attributes

findings.summary: All six identity fields are captured and recorded in both audit logs and telemetry spans.
findings.next_step: Runtime evidence: query audit records from a test run and verify zero missing values.

evidence.note: agent_type_id() computes hash from container, harness, prompt, model, config, mcp
Inputs sorted and hashed consistently
Model ID included in hash

findings.summary: Type ID is computed from container digest, harness files, system prompt, model ID, config, and MCP servers. Same inputs yield same ID.
findings.next_step: Runtime: verify changing each input changes the ID, and same manifest gives same ID.

evidence.note: identity dict built in harness from configuration, not from model
Tenant taken from identity dict (trusted), not from model input

findings.summary: Identity is assigned in the trusted execution layer (harness), not from untrusted input.
findings.next_step: Runtime: send fake tenant labels in arguments and verify they're rejected or replaced.

evidence.note: Ownership info: Accountable and Operational owner listed

findings.summary: Basic ownership info exists but no service catalog or operational lookup system is visible.
findings.next_step: Verify an operator can find the manifest, owners, and running instances from a trace ID or action ID.

evidence.note: No sub-agents spawned; only one model call per run

findings.summary: The agent does not start sub-agents.
findings.next_step: Governance approval of N/A status.

evidence.note: Only one model configured: claude-3-5-sonnet-latest
Single model call with no helper models

findings.summary: Only one model (Claude) is used. No helper models, judges, or rerankers.
findings.next_step: If helper models are added, each must have its own type ID and error handling.

evidence.note: No manifest file listing release artifacts
Model ID is -latest alias, not a pinned version
MCP servers have no versions specified

findings.summary: No release manifest file exists. Model and MCP server versions are not pinned.
findings.next_step: Create .brace/manifest.yaml listing container digest, harness version, system prompt hash, model version (pinned), MCP server versions, and tools.

evidence.note: Deploy via kubectl apply (no CI/CD process mentioned)

findings.summary: No visible review process for manifest or policy changes. Need to verify CODEOWNERS and branch protection.
findings.next_step: Check CODEOWNERS for prompts, policy, and manifest files. Verify branch protection blocks force-push and requires reviews.

evidence.note: IMAGE_DIGEST comes from pod annotation (can be wrong)
Image deployed by :latest tag, not digest

findings.summary: Type ID is computed from IMAGE_DIGEST annotation, but the actual deployed image may differ. Image is referenced by mutable tag.
findings.next_step: Pin image by digest in deployment. Verify running image digest matches approved manifest.

findings.summary: No drift detection rules are visible in the code. Likely in external monitoring system.
findings.next_step: Verify: prompt changes, MCP server changes, egress policy changes are detected and trigger alerts.

evidence.note: Model: claude-3-5-sonnet-latest (mutable alias)
MCP versions use npx -y (latest)

findings.summary: Model and dependency versions are not pinned. Using -latest and npx -y means the running version can change without code changes.
findings.next_step: Pin all dependencies: model ID (request specific version), lockfile with exact package versions, MCP server versions. Document any alias vs. snapshot distinction.

findings.summary: No release test suite is visible. Tests for attack cases, injection containment, and stop path are not shown.
findings.next_step: Verify a release test suite exists that includes: allowed tasks, destructive-action denials, injection tests, and kill switch tests. Block promotion on failures.

findings.summary: No rollback procedure is documented in the repository.
findings.next_step: Document rollback steps. Verify previous image digests are retained and that credentials don't get restored on rollback.

evidence.note: agent.type.id is emitted in spans
Type ID is deterministic and can link to config

findings.summary: Type ID is linked to execution via telemetry. Manifest lookup is possible via type ID.
findings.next_step: Runtime: verify traces carry type ID and that manifest is retrievable from that ID.

evidence.note: Ownership info provided
External services: Zendesk, Stripe, Gmail

findings.summary: External dependencies (Zendesk, Stripe, Gmail, Qdrant, Database, Redis) are used, but no responsibility table is in the repo.
findings.next_step: Create .brace/dependencies.yaml listing each external service, the agent-team owner, and the vendor/platform owner for each control.

evidence.note: @helpwise-labs/zendesk-mcp has no version
@stripe/mcp has no version
gmail-mcp-server has no version
Using npx -y downloads latest every time

findings.summary: Dependencies have no pinned versions. MCP servers are fetched by name without version pins.
findings.next_step: Pin MCP server versions. Create a lockfile or add version pins to .mcp.json. Scan for known vulnerabilities in pinned versions.

evidence.note: list_tools called but no fingerprint comparison

findings.summary: No fingerprint comparison on tool load. Cached tool definitions could differ from server.
findings.next_step: Implement fingerprint hashing of tool descriptions and schemas. Re-check on every load and block if fingerprint doesn't match.

evidence.note: Tool descriptions inserted directly into Anthropic tool list with no sanitization
inputSchema passed directly with no inspection

findings.summary: Tool metadata (names, descriptions, schemas) from MCP servers are not scanned for hidden instructions or injection payloads before presenting to the model.
findings.next_step: Implement a scanner for tool metadata: check for hidden characters, role overrides, length limits, and references to other tools. Reject suspicious metadata.

evidence.note: Tools indexed by bare name only: self.tool_index[tool.name] = server_name
Tool name passed to model without server namespace

findings.summary: Tools are indexed by bare name, not by server identity. A new server could add a tool with the same name as an existing one, silently overwriting the entry.
findings.next_step: Namespace tools by server identity (e.g. zendesk/create_ticket). Warn on duplicate or lookalike names across servers.

evidence.note: No gateway between agent and MCP servers; direct process launch
MCP servers launched as subprocesses with npx
User token passed directly to MCP server environment
No rate limiting or per-call validation of MCP responses

findings.summary: No gateway or enforcement layer between agent and MCP tools. User token is passed directly. No rate limits or response validation.
findings.next_step: Implement an MCP gateway that: authenticates/authorizes each call, validates responses, enforces rate limits, and uses separate credentials.

evidence.note: No A2A server or peer agent endpoint

findings.summary: The agent does not receive messages from other agents.
findings.next_step: Governance approval of N/A status.

evidence.note: No sub-agents or delegation

findings.summary: The agent does not delegate to sub-agents or peers.
findings.next_step: Governance approval of N/A status.

evidence.note: Kill switch halts the main loop
Kill switch checked before each iteration

findings.summary: Kill switch stops the main loop. No sub-agents or workers to cascade to.
findings.next_step: Runtime: verify stop within set time and that MCP tool calls are properly cancelled.

evidence.note: All six identity fields recorded for every action
Identity fields emitted in traces

findings.summary: Identity fields are consistently recorded in audit logs and telemetry.
findings.next_step: Runtime: merge audit logs across services and verify no gaps in identity attribution.

evidence.note: Audit logs written to Postgres database

findings.summary: Audit is stored in Postgres, but retention policy, access controls, and integrity checks are not visible in code.
findings.next_step: Verify: audit retention at least 6 months, durable buffering, alerts on delivery failures, and immutable storage (append-only or WORM).

findings.summary: No fleet incident response procedures are visible in the repository.
findings.next_step: Verify: a way to find which instances use a given tool/version, quarantine controls, and incident runbooks.
